evals.prompt: I have a new Git project that will contain a .env file and config/secrets.yml for storing database passwords and API keys. I want to use git-crypt to encrypt these files, then share the key with my colleague Wang (GPG email: wang@example.com). Walk me through the setup step by step.
evals.expected_output: Should provide complete steps: git-crypt init, write .gitattributes (with encryption rules for .env and config/secrets.yml plus the .gitattributes exclusion rule), commit .gitattributes before adding sensitive files, use git-crypt add-gpg-user to grant access to the colleague

assertions.text: Shows correct .gitattributes with filter=git-crypt diff=git-crypt syntax
Emphasizes that .gitattributes must be committed BEFORE adding sensitive files
Uses git-crypt add-gpg-user to share access with the colleague

evals.prompt: My repo already has a credentials/ directory with several JSON files containing tokens for various services. They were pushed in plaintext without any encryption. Now I want to encrypt that directory with git-crypt. How should I handle this? What about the leaked history?
evals.expected_output: Should explain: 1) set up .gitattributes with credentials/** rule; 2) use git-crypt status -f to fix; 3) warn that plaintext remains in history and suggest BFG Repo-Cleaner to clean it; 4) advise immediate rotation of exposed tokens

assertions.text: Mentions git-crypt status -f to fix/encrypt files that should be encrypted
Uses credentials/** (double star) not credentials/* for recursive directory encryption
Warns that plaintext versions remain in Git history even after encryption
Suggests BFG Repo-Cleaner or git filter-branch to clean history

evals.prompt: Our team has frontend and backend groups. Frontend needs access to frontend/config/.env, backend needs access to backend/secrets/ for database connection info. I don't want frontend to see backend's database passwords, and I don't want backend to see frontend's third-party API keys. Can git-crypt do this? How do I set it up?
evals.expected_output: Should introduce git-crypt's multiple key feature: create named keys with git-crypt init -k frontend and git-crypt init -k backend, use filter=git-crypt-frontend and filter=git-crypt-backend in .gitattributes, then use add-gpg-user -k to grant per-key access to different users

assertions.text: Uses git-crypt init -k to create named keys (e.g. frontend, backend)
Uses filter=git-crypt-KEYNAME syntax in .gitattributes (not just filter=git-crypt)
Uses git-crypt add-gpg-user -k KEYNAME to grant per-key access
Explains that git-crypt unlock auto-detects which key the user has access to
